Hmm, there's an issue. When I use `{:<10}`, the pattern becomes `([^\s]{10,}) *` which requires at least 10 non-whitespace characters. But "hello" only has 5 characters.

Wait, looking at the width handling: `{:<10}` means left-align with width 10. The old behavior was that it would match at least 10 characters. But now with my change for `<` alignment, it uses `[^\s]{10,}` which also requires at least 10 non-whitespace chars. That seems correct actually - the width specifies minimum characters.

But wait, in the original test output, `{:5}` (right-aligned by default) gave `'hello'` from search, not the full string. Let me re-check what the expected behavior should be...

Actually, looking at the requirement again: "Left- and center-aligned search operations must consume input up to the next space character." This suggests that for `{:<}` and `{:^}`, even without a width, they should stop at whitespace. With a width like `{:<10}`, maybe the width still applies?
